name: USS Iwo Jima (LPH-2), Iwo Jima-class amphibious assault ship, as in the early 1960s

published.source: en.wikipedia 'Iwo Jima-class amphibious assault ship' / Friedman, U.S. Amphibious Ships and Craft: 592 ft (180.4 m) overall, 84 ft (25.6 m) waterline beam, 105 ft (32 m) across the flight deck, 27 ft (8.2 m) draught; beam here is the WATERLINE beam (the model's Y extent is the 52.8 m from lift tip to lift tip)

must_show: one long flush flight deck x -90.2 .. +90.2, 32 m wide (y +-16), flat top at z 18.3, a BLUNT ROUND BOW forward of x +60 and a square stern with its corners cut back 3.2 m (x -86.8 .. -90.2) [P][B]; no angled deck, catapults or wires

the island on the STARBOARD edge, x -14.4 .. +8.6, inboard face y -8.2, outboard y -16.7, in stepped tiers to z 31.5 (13.2 m over the deck) with two window bands at 5-6 and 8-9 m over the deck and chamfered forward corners [P][F]
the stack at the island's after end, x -13.4 .. -8.0, head z 33.1 with a dark cap [T]

a single pole mast at x -2.2, y -12.6 off the island roof with the SPS-10 bar on a platform at z 35.9, the main yard at z 39.9 and a top yard at z 43.7, and the BEDSPRING air-search array at its head (z 46.8 .. 50.0) [F]

PORT deck-edge lift x +1.5 .. +20.0, platform out to y +26.4, hung outboard of a 2 m chamfered cut in the deck edge, the hangar opening dark in the side behind it (x +4.5 .. +17.0, z 8.6 .. 17.4) [O][P][B]
STARBOARD deck-edge lift abaft the island, x -46.5 .. -28.0, out to y -26.4, the same hangar opening behind it [P][T]

two twin 3in/50 mounts in round tubs in tandem on the starboard deck edge forward of the island, centres x +21.0 and +13.9 at y -17.2, on a sponson x +9.4 .. +25.6 just under the deck (floor z 17.3) [O][F][P]
two more twin 3in/50 in round tubs set into the stern corners under the deck, centres x -86.85, y +-12.0, floor z 13.7, each on a conical knee into the transom [T][S]
the wineglass transom at x -87.6 (waterline) raking aft to -87.9 at the gallery deck, two large stern ports at z 7.6, y +-5.4 [T][S]
a strongly flared Essex-like bow over a curved raked stem with no bulb: stem at x +84.0 on the waterline, +87.3 at z 8.6, +89.7 at the gallery deck z 17.4 [N][B][P]
catwalks with a rail on stanchions and the canted safety net along the deck edges at z 17.3 .. 18.0, white raft canisters on racks under the deck edge at z 14.9 [S][P]

the 1962 deck markings: eight big spot rings 17.4 m across in two staggered rows (y +7.3 / -7.0) on dark deck grey, e.g. at x +72, +57, +40, +23, -6, -37, -56, -72 [O][T]; no hull number, name or flags
one screw at x -82.2, z -5.6 with one rudder (x -87.2 .. -84.0) and a skeg (x -80.5 .. -56) [published: one shaft]

landmarks.name: flight deck forward end
landmarks.note: [P] deck ends at 4.4 px/m (+-0.5 m); the published 180.4 m overall

landmarks.name: starboard lift after end

landmarks.name: bedspring top
landmarks.note: [F][P]: the bedspring's top 31.7 m over the deck (+-1.5 m, as the header's NOT CONFIRMED says)

landmarks.name: stem at the waterline
